cds.text: Understand that compound sentences link two or more independent clauses, usually with a coordinating conjunction, to connect ideas
Understand that a clause is a unit of grammar, usually with a subject and verb that must agree
Understand that complex sentences have one independent clause and at least one dependent clause, joined by subordinating conjunctions to show time and cause
Understand that nouns can extend into noun groups with articles and adjectives, and verbs can form verb groups
Understand how verbs represent processes of doing, feeling, thinking, saying and relating
Investigate how quoted (direct) and reported (indirect) speech are used
Understand that verbs are anchored in time through tense
Understand how adverb groups and prepositional phrases give circumstantial details about an activity
Understand past, present and future tenses and their impact on meaning in a sentence
Understand that images add to or multiply the meanings of a text
Identify how images extend the meaning of a text
Explore the effect of framing, element placement and salience on the composition of still and moving images
Experiment with and begin making conscious vocabulary choices to suit the topic
Extend topic-specific and technical vocabulary, and know that words can have different meanings in different contexts
Expand vocabulary by exploring synonyms and antonyms and using words met in a range of sources

sentences.text: {{S}} explains how word choices can make writing entertaining or informative in both fiction and non-fiction texts.
{{S}} selects words that persuade the reader and uses language that creates emotion in poetry.
{{S}} considers {{pos}} word choices carefully to make {{pos}} writing more engaging for the reader.
{{S}} explains how vocabulary choices can enhance the entertainment value of narratives.
{{S}} applies known vocabulary effectively and is beginning to experiment with descriptive language to add detail.
{{S}} uses a varied vocabulary in {{pos}} own writing.
{{S}} experiments with different styles and incorporates vocabulary drawn from other texts.
{{S}} recognises that words can have multiple meanings and applies this knowledge to understand and create texts.
{{S}} understands that words can have multiple meanings and uses a varied vocabulary.
{{S}} brainstorms words that have the same or opposite meaning and uses these to avoid repetition.
{{S}} talks about the meaning of figurative language, such as similes and idioms.
